title: How to Get Oil in Scrap Mechanic
description: Collect Oil with the correct bucket or pump route, convert Oil Buckets into Crude Oil, and turn that into Gasoline without chasing unsupported pond or vent rumors.
imageAlt: Scrap Mechanic shoreline route used for oil collection planning
quickAnswer: If you need to know how to get oil in Scrap Mechanic, start by separating three terms: Oil is the wiki resource topic, Oil Bucket is the carried container state, and Crude Oil is the crafting input. Collect Oil Buckets directly or automate intake with a Vacuum Pump and storage, then craft 1 Oil Bucket into 5 Crude Oil at the Craftbot. Convert 5 Crude Oil into 5 Gasoline when fuel is the goal, and reserve a return-trip stack before spending the batch on engines or suspension.

media.alt: Scrap Mechanic Oil resource guide icon for crude oil crafting
media.caption: Use the Oil wiki entry for the item definition, then use this guide for the acquisition route and conversion checkpoints.

media.alt: Scrap Mechanic Gasoline crafted from Crude Oil
media.caption: Gasoline is the practical reason to collect Crude Oil early. Do not spend the whole batch before reserving return-trip fuel.

Vacuum Pump in In mode plus compatible storage
Repository part data lists Crude Oil as a supported pump target.
Craftbot converts 5 Crude Oil to 5 Gasoline; Portable Crafter and Workbench convert 1 to 1.

sections.heading: How to Get Oil in Scrap Mechanic: quick answer
paragraphs: The site data separates three terms that players often collapse into one search: Oil is the wiki resource topic, Oil Bucket is the carried container state, and Crude Oil is the crafting input used by fuel and industrial recipes.
If a guide tells you to refine Oil in an extra station, ignore it for this build. The current repository recipe set uses Craftbot, Portable Crafter, and Workbench conversions.

sections.heading: How to Get Oil in Scrap Mechanic by hand
steps: Leave base with enough Gasoline for the outbound and return drive.
Keep storage empty enough for Oil Buckets or later Crude Oil stacks.
Collect the Oil Bucket state first; do not convert it until you know the final use.
Return to the Craftbot before crafting fuel so the conversion happens beside storage.
Convert only the portion needed for Gasoline, suspension, or engine work.
paragraphs: Run the manual route when the base is still light and fuel is scarce. Bring at least one empty Oil Bucket slot, park the vehicle where it can be turned around without reversing through bots, and collect only what you can bring home cleanly. The failure state is not the collection click; it is overextending until the return trip costs more fuel than the oil run produced.

Use visual confirmation instead of inherited map claims. Current site data supports Oil Bucket and Crude Oil handling, but it does not support fixed numeric yields, fixed coordinates, or extra conversion stations. Treat each collection point as a route checkpoint: identify it, collect, mark the road back, and leave before night pressure turns a resource run into a vehicle recovery job.

sections.heading: How to Get Oil in Scrap Mechanic with a Vacuum Pump
paragraphs: Vacuum Pump data lists In and Out modes and includes Crude Oil as a supported collection target. The pump still needs the right direction, a compatible container, a valid intake position, and free capacity.
Do not build a giant extractor first. Test a direct pump-to-storage line, confirm one transfer, then scale the route.

The Vacuum Pump route is for repeatability, not magic output. The part can collect Crude Oil, but it still needs the same practical checks as any fluid intake: correct In mode, a valid intake position, storage with free capacity, and a connection path that is not blocked by a reversed pump or full container.

Test the pump with a small container before building a full outpost. If one cycle does not move the resource into storage, do not add more pipes yet. Check pump direction, storage capacity, and the control signal. Scaling a broken intake only hides the first failed condition under more parts.
bullets: If the pump animates but collects nothing, check In mode and intake placement first.
If storage stays empty, connect one pump directly to one empty container and remove the pipe chain from the test.
If the shoreline is inconsistent, move the intake and retest rather than declaring a fixed spawn coordinate.

sections.heading: Oil route setup before leaving base
paragraphs: The best oil run starts at the garage, not at the collection point. Put one chest or vehicle container on the route vehicle, carry repair material, and leave one inventory row empty for emergency pickups. If the route crosses rough ground, lower speed beats top speed because tipped vehicles burn more time than slow vehicles.

Keep the first conversion close to storage. Crafting Oil Bucket into Crude Oil at the Craftbot gives a clean 1 to 5 inventory result, while the common Gasoline conversion uses 5 Crude Oil into 5 Gasoline. That makes the minimum useful fuel batch easy to audit: one Oil Bucket can become one five-unit Crude Oil batch, and that batch can become one five-unit Gasoline batch if fuel is the only target.
bullets: Reserve fuel for the return drive before crafting anything else.
Do not mix Oil Buckets, Crude Oil, and Gasoline in one unlabeled chest.
Keep one unconverted batch if the next build needs Crude Oil directly.
Use the Recipes directory when the target part matters more than raw fuel.

sections.heading: Oil image checkpoints and common misreads
paragraphs: The Oil media block uses the resource icon and Gasoline icon deliberately. The icon pair teaches the actual decision: collect and hold the resource state first, then decide whether the output becomes Crude Oil stock or immediate Gasoline. A scenic screenshot would be less useful here because generated worlds can move the route, while the item-state distinction never stops mattering.

Do not read the Gasoline image as proof that every oil trip should become fuel. Gas Engine work, Thruster experiments, and long scouting routes need Gasoline; some crafting and progression checks need the intermediate resource. Convert after the plan is clear, not because the Craftbot menu is open.

sections.heading: Common oil mistakes
bullets: Do not search for an extra-station conversion; it is not in the current recipe path.
Do not spend every Crude Oil stack on decorative or side recipes before reserving Gasoline.
Do not quote fixed oil field yields unless you tested that exact current-version world state.

sections.heading: Frequently asked questions
bullets: How do you collect oil in Scrap Mechanic? Use an Oil Bucket route or a Vacuum Pump intake with compatible storage, then convert Oil Bucket into Crude Oil if needed.
Where is Crude Oil located? The repository supports collection routing but does not provide universal fixed coordinates, so use visible liquid-source routing and storage tests.
Can a Vacuum Pump collect oil? Yes, the current Vacuum Pump data lists Crude Oil as a supported In-mode target.
What is Crude Oil used for? Gasoline, early suspension and gas-engine recipes, blocks, and some later decorative or utility recipes.

title: How to Get Water in Scrap Mechanic
description: Use the starter Water Bucket, Craftbot bucket recipe, Vacuum Pump storage, and Water Cannon delivery for ship fires, crops, and farm builds.
imageAlt: Scrap Mechanic farm route where water collection and delivery matter
quickAnswer: If you need to know how to get water in Scrap Mechanic, use a filled Water Bucket for the first job and a Vacuum Pump plus Water Container for repeat work. The Crash Site bucket handles the opening fires and early crops. Later, craft a Water Container, set a submerged Vacuum Pump to In mode, connect storage, and feed a Water Cannon only after the container can fill and drain on command.

media.alt: Scrap Mechanic Water Bucket location and water collection guide
media.caption: The Water Bucket is the first verified water tool and remains the fallback when automation fails.

media.alt: Scrap Mechanic Water Container for farm water storage
media.caption: Water Container storage matters before a Water Cannon can deliver clean farming cycles.

sections.heading: How to Get Water in Scrap Mechanic: quick answer
paragraphs: The early route is not complicated: pick up the Crash Site Water Bucket, fill it at the pond, and repeat the trip for each marked ship fire or crop plot.
Automation begins only when you have a Water Container and a pump line that has passed a one-transfer test.

sections.heading: How to Get Water in Scrap Mechanic with a Water Bucket
steps: Enter the crashed ship first so the opening objective activates.
Follow the path opposite the ship entrance to the pond beside the farming setup.
Pick up the Water Bucket at the pond edge.
Use the bucket on open water, then throw the filled bucket at the marked fire or dry crop plot.
Refill after each use. A filled bucket becomes empty after throwing water.
paragraphs: The bucket route is still the correct first answer because it has the fewest failure points. Find or craft the bucket, fill it from open water, throw the water at the marked fire or crop, and refill. The only timing mistake is trying to scale farming before the bucket loop is proven and before spare seeds are protected.

Use the bucket as a diagnostic tool after automation exists. If a crop row accepts bucket water but the Water Cannon misses, the crop is not the problem. The failure is delivery angle, storage, pump direction, or control timing. That distinction saves a full rebuild.

sections.heading: How to Get Water in Scrap Mechanic with a Vacuum Pump
paragraphs: The pump does not replace storage. It moves water only when the intake, mode, control signal, and connected container are all valid.
Build the first test as a short direct line. A long pipe chain hides the real fault when the pump is reversed or the container is full.

The pump route needs a clean intake chain. Start with the smallest complete circuit: Vacuum Pump in In mode, valid water contact, one Water Container, and one switch or button. Do not add pistons, sensors, or moving gantries until one manual trigger fills storage.

When the container stays empty, audit the system in order. First check that the pump direction is In. Second, check that the intake is actually placed where the game accepts water. Third, check that the container is connected and has capacity. Fourth, check that your control signal reaches the pump. Randomly rotating parts after each test creates new variables and makes the next failure harder to read.
bullets: Pump mode: In for collection from water.
Storage: Water Container with free capacity.
Delivery: Water Cannon or bucket refill after storage is confirmed.

sections.heading: How to Get Water in Scrap Mechanic into a Water Cannon
steps: Fill a Water Container with a bucket or pump intake.
Connect the Water Cannon to the container.
Connect a Button, Switch, Sensor, or Controller logic line for activation.
Fire one shot at one crop plot before moving the cannon on a piston or vehicle.
Only scale the watering arm after the single-shot test waters the intended plot.
paragraphs: Treat the Water Cannon as delivery, not storage. The reliable chain is source, pump, Water Container, cannon, trigger. If the cannon fires dry, step backward through the chain instead of rebuilding the cannon mount. A dry cannon usually means the container never filled, the connection is wrong, or the trigger is firing before water reaches the line.

For crop rows, aim for coverage you can observe. One short row is enough for the first pass. Fire once, walk the row, and confirm every plot received water before you automate movement. A piston or controller can make the same mistake faster; it cannot fix a bad water angle.

sections.heading: Water route setup before farming automation
paragraphs: A good water setup has a manual fallback. Keep a filled bucket near the farm even after the pump works, because raids, vehicle impacts, and accidental rewiring can interrupt the automatic line. The goal is not to remove the bucket forever; the goal is to stop hand-watering from being the only way the farm survives.

Build in layers. First prove storage. Then prove one Water Cannon shot. Then prove one crop row. Only after those three checks should you add controller timing, piston travel, or sensors. This order makes the failure visible at the exact layer where it starts.
steps: Fill one Water Bucket by hand and verify the crop or objective accepts water.
Fill one Water Container from a fixed Vacuum Pump.
Fire one Water Cannon shot from the filled container.
Water one short crop row and inspect every plot.
Add movement automation only after the fixed test passes.

sections.heading: Water image checkpoints and common misreads
paragraphs: The Water Bucket image marks the first verified tool. It belongs early in the page because it answers the opening player problem: put out the ship fires and keep a small crop row alive. The Water Container image marks the point where the route changes from manual carrying to stored supply.

Do not treat the container image as proof that the pump is optional. A Water Container without intake is just a tank. The container becomes useful when a pump fills it and a cannon or bucket route draws from it in a controlled cycle.

sections.heading: Frequently asked questions
bullets: How do you get a Water Container? Craft it at the Craftbot with 10 Metal Block Level 1, 5 Circuit Boards, and 4 Glue.
Can you drink water in Scrap Mechanic? This guide does not support a player-hydration claim; repository water uses are objectives, crops, and storage.
Why is my pump not collecting water? Check In mode, intake placement, free Water Container capacity, and direct connection before changing the whole build.
Can a bucket refill from storage? Yes, the Water Bucket data lists open water or a filled Water Container as refill sources.

title: How to Get Battery in Scrap Mechanic
description: Get the normal Battery item through verified loot, Craftbot recipes, and routing discipline while keeping Master Battery quest objects separate.
imageAlt: Scrap Mechanic powered base route for Battery planning
quickAnswer: If you are searching how to get battery in Scrap Mechanic, use the normal Battery item route, not the Master Battery quest route. Loot early Batteries conservatively, then craft 10 Batteries at the Craftbot from 5 Metal Block Level 1, 1 Glow, and 5 Chemicals when the recipe is available. The Battery item powers electric systems and appears in electrical crafting chains; the Master Battery is a fixed progression object and should not be planned as fuel.

media.alt: Scrap Mechanic Battery crafting and electric engine guide
media.caption: Normal Batteries power electric systems and stack separately from fixed Master Battery quest objects.

media.alt: Scrap Mechanic Master Battery is not the same as normal Battery
media.caption: Master Batteries are progression items. Do not put them in the same mental bucket as electric-engine fuel.

tables.caption: Battery quick reference
tables.note: No vanilla recharge-station or spent-battery loop is used in this guide. Treat charging claims as mod-specific until proven otherwise.

tables.caption: Battery recipe and consumers
rows: Output from Metal 1, Glow, and Chemicals
Consumes 5 Batteries in the recipe and then uses Batteries as power

sections.heading: How to Get Battery in Scrap Mechanic: quick answer
paragraphs: The normal Battery item is consumable power. The Master Battery is a fixed story/progression object used by the crashed ship and Mechanic Station route.
If a route tells you to recharge spent Batteries in vanilla Survival, stop and check the mod list. The current repository data has no recharge-station entry and no spent-battery mechanic.

sections.heading: How to Get Battery in Scrap Mechanic from loot
paragraphs: The item wiki describes Batteries as normal electric-system power and separates them from Master Batteries. Loot routes are useful early, but the guide should not promise guaranteed drops where the current data does not provide exact tables.
Bring Batteries home before committing to an electric vehicle. A loose handful in inventory disappears quickly once test driving begins.

Looted Battery stacks are best treated as runway, not income. Spend the first few only when the build immediately solves a movement, power, or progression problem. If a part can wait until the Craftbot recipe is online, let it wait. Running out of Battery items before the electric build is finished creates the worst kind of stop: the vehicle looks complete but cannot do the job.

Separate every Master Battery prompt from the normal Battery item. The crashed ship and Mechanic Station objectives use fixed Master Battery objects, while electric systems consume the normal item. Mixing those names in storage labels, notes, or guide planning is the main reason battery routes look inconsistent.

sections.heading: How to Get Battery in Scrap Mechanic at the Craftbot
steps: Stabilize Metal Block Level 1 supply first.
Collect Chemicals and keep them away from water or fuel storage.
Reserve Glow specifically for the Battery batch instead of spending it on side recipes.
Craft Battery x10 at the Craftbot.
Store the batch beside the electric machine that will consume it.
paragraphs: The verified Craftbot recipe is the clean fallback: 5 Metal Block Level 1, 1 Glow, and 5 Chemicals produce 10 Battery items. That output size matters. Craft in tens, then divide the batch between active electric systems, recipe requirements, and a reserve stack. Do not feed every new Battery into the first experimental engine test.

Chemicals are the gating ingredient in practice. Before crafting, check whether the next project actually needs electric power or whether a gas setup will solve the route with resources you already have. A battery craft is efficient when it unlocks a system; it is wasteful when it becomes a decorative stockpile beside an unfinished build.

sections.heading: What Batteries are used for
bullets: Electric Engine systems that need controlled battery-powered movement.
Battery Container routing for larger electric builds.
Crafting ingredients for electrical or powered objects such as Power Station and Broken Microwave.
Recovery stock when a vehicle or machine consumes more than expected during testing.
paragraphs: A Battery Container changes logistics, not the source of power. It can store more Battery items and load them into connected Electric Engines and compatible interactive parts. That makes it useful on vehicles or machines that need a managed supply, but it does not turn Master Batteries into fuel and it does not prove a vanilla recharge loop.

For electric vehicles, test consumption under load. A vehicle that works on flat ground can still drain the supply too quickly while climbing or hauling. Run a short route, return to base, and record how many Battery items disappeared before expanding the build.

sections.heading: Battery route setup before electric builds
paragraphs: The right battery route starts with the target machine. List the Electric Engine, Battery Container, switches, and any other interactive parts before crafting the batch. Then decide how many Battery items are for testing and how many are reserved for the actual trip. Testing without a reserve is how a half-built electric vehicle strands itself at the edge of the base.

If the build is still experimental, use a short loop. Drive out, turn, climb one slope, return, and check consumption. That small route gives better data than a long expedition because every missing Battery can be tied to one test condition.
bullets: Label normal Battery storage separately from Master Battery quest notes.
Craft in 10-item batches and reserve part of each batch.
Do not assume charging unless a mod or future patch explicitly adds it.
Use Gasoline systems when the route needs cheap early movement more than controlled electric power.

sections.heading: Battery image checkpoints and common misreads
paragraphs: The normal Battery image is the page anchor because it is the item players spend in electric systems. The Master Battery image is included as a warning, not as a source route. The two icons look like progression resources, but they belong to different loops.

When an electric build fails, check the normal Battery supply before blaming the engine. A missing connection, empty Battery Container, or no reserve stack can all look like a broken machine from the driver's seat.

sections.heading: Frequently asked questions
bullets: Where can you find Batteries early? Treat early Batteries as loot and exploration stock, but do not assume a guaranteed route unless the current save shows it.
What is the Battery recipe? Craftbot: 5 Metal Block Level 1, 1 Glow, and 5 Chemicals for 10 Batteries.
Can you charge Batteries? Not in the verified vanilla data used here. Charging belongs to mods or unsupported claims until proven otherwise.
Is a Master Battery the same as a Battery? No. Master Batteries are fixed progression objects; normal Batteries power electric systems.

title: How to Get Schematics in Scrap Mechanic
description: Get Schematic Boxes, scan them at Schematicbot, unlock recipes, and troubleshoot missing unlocks using verified station and drop data.
imageAlt: Scrap Mechanic 1.0 progression scene for schematic unlock planning
quickAnswer: If you need to know how to get schematics in Scrap Mechanic, collect Schematic Boxes, scan eligible blue-icon parts, complete verified quest or trader unlocks, and register the result at the Schematicbot. A Schematic Box scan consumes one box and unlocks one random eligible recipe for the save. A blue-icon part scan is exact: bring the part, scan it, then confirm the recipe at the correct crafting station.

media.caption: Each Schematic Box scan consumes one box and registers one random eligible recipe in the save.

media.alt: Scrap Mechanic Schematicbot recipe unlock station guide
media.caption: The Schematicbot is a fixed station. It scans boxes or eligible blue-icon parts; it is not a movable base machine.

sections.heading: How to Get Schematics in Scrap Mechanic: quick answer
paragraphs: Do not stop at picking up a Schematic Box. The useful state is the registered recipe after the Schematicbot scan and final unlock confirmation.
The box does not produce a finished item. It opens a recipe, and the item still needs its normal station, materials, and craft time.

sections.heading: How to Get Schematics in Scrap Mechanic from Schematic Boxes
steps: Get Schematic Boxes from Farmers Hideout exchange, Tapebot drops, crate routes, or fixed placed-box layouts when found.
Carry the box stack to a Schematicbot station.
Scan one box and wait for the roughly two-second scan.
Confirm the unlock after the scan completes.
Open the Craftbot or Saw Table list and find the newly available recipe.
paragraphs: Use Schematic Boxes when you are building the general recipe pool. The box route is not targeted; it is controlled randomness. That means one box should never be promised as the exact missing recipe unless the source data says the pool is already constrained. Scan the box, record the unlock, and then check the Craftbot or Saw Table before assuming the reward failed.

The current data gives the Schematic Box a clear identity: it stacks to 10, is consumed per scan, and can come from verified drop or trade sources. The page table keeps those sources in one place so the route is based on source category and chance, not invented map coordinates.

sections.heading: How to Get Schematics in Scrap Mechanic from part scans
paragraphs: An eligible part with the blue schematic icon is the precision route. Scan it when you care about that exact recipe more than random pool efficiency.
The current Schematicbot data says the part is not consumed. Once the recipe is unlocked, that part stops appearing as an available scan input.

Part scanning solves a different problem. When the item has a blue icon and the Schematicbot accepts it, the scan is exact rather than random. That makes part scans better for a specific missing build component, while Schematic Boxes are better for widening the recipe pool.

Keep the part scan close to storage if possible. After registration, go straight to the matching crafting station and confirm the recipe appears. If the recipe is visible but cannot be made, the issue is materials or station access, not schematic acquisition.

sections.heading: How to use the Schematicbot
bullets: Inputs: blue-icon part or Schematic Box.
Box scan: random eligible recipe and one box consumed.
Part scan: exact matching recipe and part preserved.
Visible choices: three inputs at a time; use arrows if more are available.
Locations: kiosk layouts and Mining Hub. Bring the input to the station; the station is fixed.
paragraphs: The Schematicbot is a registration station. Stand close enough to interact, choose the accepted input, and wait for the scan to complete before leaving. A half-finished interaction is not the same as a registered unlock, so watch for the recipe result instead of assuming the box leaving your inventory is the final proof.

For multiplayer saves, let the host verify the unlock after scanning. The current site data describes unlock scope at the save level, but host state is still the practical place to diagnose missing recipes. If a client cannot see the recipe, have the host check the station before rescanning another box.

sections.heading: Schematic route setup before scanning
paragraphs: Prepare a small scan log. Write down the source, the item scanned, and the recipe that appears. This sounds excessive until two boxes in a row unlock recipes you did not need and you cannot remember whether the third box was actually scanned. A simple log also makes mod and version troubleshooting cleaner.

Do not carry every box into a risky route. Scan at a known station, move the unlocked recipe into the build plan, then go back out for more sources. Losing an unscanned box is an inventory loss; losing track of a registered recipe is an information problem.
steps: Collect one verified Schematic Box or one eligible blue-icon part.
Bring it to a Schematicbot location such as a kiosk layout or Mining Hub station.
Scan one item at a time and wait for the unlock result.
Check the correct Craftbot or Saw Table recipe list.
Record the unlock before scanning the next source.

sections.heading: Schematic image checkpoints and common misreads
paragraphs: The Schematic Box image marks random-pool progression. The Schematicbot image marks registration. Put together, they show the full loop: obtain a valid source, scan it, then verify the recipe at the station. Skipping the verification step is the fastest way to misdiagnose a normal material shortage as a schematic bug.
Do not read the Schematicbot image as a shop interface. The current route is scan and register first, then craft elsewhere when the recipe and materials are available.

sections.heading: Why the recipe is not showing
bullets: You left after the scan timer and did not press the final unlock control.
You checked the wrong station; the random pool can include Craftbot and Saw Table outputs.
The recipe was already unlocked before the scan.
The box pool is exhausted in this save, so carried boxes may stop appearing as usable inputs.
In multiplayer, let the host complete one scan and then recheck the shared recipe list.

sections.heading: Frequently asked questions
bullets: Where do you find Schematic Boxes? Farmers Hideout trades, Tapebot drops, crate rewards, and specific placed-box layouts are verified in the repository data.
What does the Schematicbot do? It registers recipe unlocks from boxes or eligible blue-icon parts.
Can you lose a schematic unlock? The registered recipe is shared by the save; losing an unscanned box is not the same as losing an unlocked recipe.
Do Schematicbots sell rotating stock? No. The current data describes fixed stations and separate trader recipe offers, not regional stock.

title: Beginner Guide - Crash Site to Mechanic Station
description: Complete the opening ship recovery in order: find the Water Bucket, extinguish three marked fires, install the first Master Battery, reconnect the console, take the Logbook, and only then choose a farm or first-car branch.
imageAlt: Mechanics working inside a powered Scrap Mechanic station
quickAnswer: Enter the crashed ship to start Getting Started, follow the path opposite its entrance to the pond, fill the Water Bucket, extinguish the three marked fires inside, recover the nearby Master Battery, restore ship power, reconnect the console with the Connect Tool, and take the Logbook before leaving for the Mechanic Station.

sections.heading: 1. Trigger Getting Started Inside the Ship
paragraphs: Walk into the crashed maintenance ship before looting outward. The active yellow objective is the reliable start signal: it sends you to water and later replaces completed markers with the Master Battery, console, and Logbook steps. If the pond has no useful marker yet, return to the ship interior and let Getting Started activate.
bullets: Opening fire: Water Bucket and pond water.
Later Hideout fire quest: Fire Extinguisher received after Built to Last.
These are separate objectives; an extinguisher is not required to leave the Crash Site.

sections.heading: 2. Find the Water Bucket at the Pond
paragraphs: Stand at the ship entrance and take the path running away from it. The nearby pond is grouped with a farming billboard, Soil Bags, seeds, and a planted Tomato. The Water Bucket sits at the pond edge. Use the empty bucket on the water, return to the ship, throw the splash at a marked fire, then refill for the next marked fire.

sections.heading: 3. Extinguish the Three Marked Interior Fires
steps: Carry a filled Water Bucket back through the ship entrance.
Aim at one fire carrying the active objective marker and throw the water.
Return to the pond when the bucket is empty and refill it.
Repeat until all three marked fires inside the ship are gone and the objective changes.

sections.heading: 4. Recover the First Master Battery
paragraphs: After the final marked fire is extinguished, Getting Started points toward the ruin near the Crash Site. Follow the crash debris and damaged-crate trail, clear the immediate approach, take the marked Master Battery, and carry it back to the ship socket. Do not save this battery for the Mechanic Station; the station objective marks its own battery later.

sections.heading: 5. Power the Ship, Reconnect the Console, Take the Logbook
paragraphs: Installing the Master Battery restores the crashed ship's powered opening systems and Mini Craftbot. Follow the remaining objective state instead of leaving immediately: craft the Connect Tool, make the requested console connection, then collect and open the Logbook. The ship phase is complete when the Mechanic Station waypoint can be selected in the Logbook.

sections.heading: 6. Choose Farming or Your First Car
paragraphs: The pond area already contains the pieces for a manual farming lesson, while the blue Your First Car assignment contains a twelve-state vehicle tutorial. Both are useful after Getting Started, but neither should replace the fire, battery, console, and Logbook sequence. A small farm supplies food; a simple car shortens the road trip. Choose the current bottleneck rather than trying to finish both as one oversized build.
steps: Farm branch: plant one short Tomato, Potato, or Carrot row that can be watered entirely by hand.
Vehicle branch: complete steering and power connections before adding a chest or bodywork.
Keep spare seeds away from the planted row and keep the vehicle outside the likely bot approach.

sections.heading: 7. Follow a Reversible Route to the Mechanic Station
paragraphs: Use the Logbook waypoint and the road network rather than another world's coordinates. Generated terrain changes the exact turns, but the destination is recognizable by the illuminated wrench. Record bridges and large junctions in reverse order so the Crash Site remains findable after dark. At the station, locate its separate Master Battery, restore the control panel, and build the Craftbot required by the next progression stage.

sections.heading: Opening Questions That Should Not Stop the Route
bullets: Cannot find the bucket: return to the ship, activate the fire objective, then follow the path opposite the entrance to the pond edge.
Fire will not count: target the three marked fires inside the ship, not an unmarked exterior flame.
Ship still has no power: the first Master Battery must be inserted into the crashed ship socket.
Mechanic Station still has no power: locate the second battery marked by The Mechanic Station objective.
No station waypoint: finish the console objective and open the Logbook before starting the road journey.

title: Returning Player Guide - Saves, Mods, and 1.0 Systems
description: A version-boundary checklist for old Creative and Survival worlds, Parts and Custom Game mods, schematics, multiplayer hosts, and the original launch patches through 1.0.3, with a separate current-release warning.
quickAnswer: Old Creative worlds can load in 1.0; old Survival worlds need a legacy Steam branch. Back up the complete save before switching, test Parts or Custom Game mods on a copy, and check the current 1.0.5 patch timeline before diagnosing raid, Vault, underground, welding, or Thruster problems.

sections.heading: Back Up the Whole World Before Changing a Branch
steps: Close the game so the save is not being written.
Copy the complete world to a dated folder outside the active save directory.
Record the game version, branch, host, and enabled mod list beside it.
Open a copied world first after changing branch or mod configuration.
Keep the untouched backup until quests, creations, and storage have all been checked.

sections.heading: Do Not Use a Legacy Survival World to Judge 1.0
paragraphs: The complete story, reworked world generation, Growlabs, Excavation Island, new bots, Schematicbot progression, and Scrap City Garage belong to the new Survival baseline. A legacy branch is for preserving an old world, not for sampling the complete 1.0 progression.

sections.heading: Separate Schematic Failure From Crafting Failure
steps: Confirm the box entered the inventory.
Take it to the Schematicbot and register the matching recipe.
Check the Craftbot for the exact item rather than only the schematic icon.
If no recipe appears, update past 1.0.1 and repeat on the host.
Preserve the save before removing mods or changing branches.

sections.heading: Multiplayer Retest Order
bullets: Host loads the backed-up world and performs the final quest or unlock interaction.
Clients rejoin only after the objective state is visible to the host.
Steering is tested on a simple vehicle before a complex bearing creation.
One mod category is restored at a time so a failing package has a name.

sections.heading: When the Current Patch Still Does Not Fix the Save
paragraphs: A patched engine condition does not always repair state already written into a world. Keep the affected copy, record the objective and the action immediately before it stopped, and retry from the last clean backup. Repeatedly overwriting the only world removes the evidence needed to distinguish a current bug from damaged legacy state.

title: Farming and Raid Defense Guide
description: Plan crop rows with exact 1.0 plant values, a protected seed reserve, one defended approach, and automation sized to an 8–12 plot test row.
imageAlt: A farm and growing area in Scrap Mechanic Survival
quickAnswer: Tomato and Potato count 1 each, while one Pineapple counts 1000. Calculate the planted total before watering high-value crops, keep seeds and machinery outside the bot approach, and automate only after one 8–12 plot row survives a complete water, harvest, and raid cycle.

sections.heading: Plant by Value, Not by Soil Count
paragraphs: Ten Oranges contribute 1000 plant-value points, the same calculator weight as one Pineapple and one thousand Tomatoes. A small fruit patch can therefore demand a stronger night than a broad starter field. Label rows by crop and record the count before watering so the Raid Calculator receives real numbers.

sections.heading: Protect the Recovery Layer
bullets: Store spare seeds away from the crop approach and away from harvested produce.
Keep a manual Water Bucket even after installing a Water System.
Place the vehicle outside the kill lane; it is transport, not disposable cover.
Use Metal-tier material on first-contact faces and scrap material behind it.

sections.heading: Build One Lit Kill Lane
steps: Walk the route from open terrain to the crop row before the warning.
Block side approaches without removing the mechanic's escape path.
Place hard peek cover where Tapebot shots cannot see the field center.
Stage potatoes and food behind the firing position, not beside the crops.
Repair the lane before replanting the next batch.

sections.heading: Watering Automation Is a Coverage Test
paragraphs: The FRM-03 watering baseline starts with 8–12 plots, one Water Container, one Water Cannon, two Pistons, a Controller, separate water and master controls, and an optional end Sensor. The number that matters is missed plots per pass. Speed increases only after a complete zero-miss cycle.

sections.heading: Harvest, Repair, Recalculate
steps: Clear all remaining bots and move drops out of the approach.
Inspect walls, Pipes, Pistons, and storage connections.
Return spare seeds only after the defense path is functional.
Enter the next crop counts in the Raid Calculator.
Expand one row or one automation stage—not both on the same untested night.

title: Warehouse Route - Spudguns, Farmbots, Tapebots, and Trashbot
description: A combat route with exact weapon damage, Farmbot key drops, Tapebot projectile pressure, Warehouse staging, and Trashbot phase rules.
quickAnswer: Budget at least 54 accurate Spudgun hits for a 1500 HP Farmbot, secure its guaranteed Warehouse Key, clear 40 HP Tapebots from hard cover, bank loot outside the entrance, and enter Trashbot phases ready for the eye-open damage window and five exposed-core hits.

sections.heading: Stage the Route Before the Farmbot Pull
steps: Unlock or craft the chosen Spudgun and split combat potatoes from farm-defense potatoes.
Park the cargo vehicle outside the Farmbot kite path.

Choose open ground with no dead end behind the player.
Count the ammunition again before firing the first shot.

sections.heading: Farmbot: The Key Is the Mandatory Drop
paragraphs: Every Normal Farmbot drops a Warehouse Key. Component Kits at 66.7% and Circuit Boards at 33.3% are additional rolls, not substitutes for the key. Pick the key up immediately; do not leave it exposed while chasing a smaller bot or repairing cosmetic vehicle damage.

sections.heading: Warehouse: Convert Rooms Into Single Angles
bullets: Peek from a hard corner; never fight from the center of an atrium.
Blue Tapebot shots at 55 and Red shots at 62 can erase a bad open crossing quickly.
Move valuable loot to an exterior chest between sections.
Use Glowsticks to reveal the next angle, not only the floor under the player.
Retreat to cleared space instead of backing into an unopened side room.

sections.heading: Do Not Treat Trashbot as a Larger Farmbot
paragraphs: Trashbot is controlled by attack patterns, eye state, phase health, and an exposed-core recovery sequence. Continuous fire into a closed eye wastes potatoes and hides the next projectile wall. Reload before the opening, deliver the phase damage, land five core hits, and reset movement space.

sections.heading: Extraction Is a Separate Phase
steps: Move keys and progression items to the exterior vehicle first.
Unload the current section before opening optional rooms.
Keep the return route lit and free of parked debris.
Leave when healing or miss reserve reaches the route minimum.
Repair and restock outside the combat structure.

title: First Vehicle Guide - Exact Starter Chassis
description: Build the VEH-01 starter car with a 10 × 16 footprint, 48-block frame, six bearings, four wheels, and repeatable steering and load tests.
imageAlt: A simple four-wheel vehicle driving in Scrap Mechanic
quickAnswer: Build a low 10 × 16 ladder frame from 48 Wood Block Level 1, use six Bearings for four hubs and two steering pivots, start engine power low, and pass full-lock, ditch, rollover, and one-chest tests before adding bodywork.

sections.heading: Lay Out the 48-Block Frame
steps: Build two 16-block rails.
Join them with at least three crossmembers.
Keep seat, engine, and future chest inside the wheelbase.
Leave both front corners open for steering travel.
Mark one accessible Lift point at each end.

sections.heading: Install Six Bearings by Role
paragraphs: The four wheel bearings rotate for drive; the two front pivot bearings rotate for steering. Mixing those roles produces connections that look complete but behave unpredictably. Connect the seat only to the steering pivots and engine throttle, then connect the engine only to driven wheel hubs.

sections.heading: Commission the Empty Chassis
bullets: Drive straight and reverse without adding power.
Complete a full-lock circle in both directions.
Cross a shallow ditch diagonally.
Tip the empty chassis in a safe area and recover it with the Lift.

sections.heading: Load One Chest, Then Repeat the Tests
paragraphs: A Large Chest changes mass distribution even when the body looks symmetrical. Mount it low, inside the wheelbase, and closer to the steering axle if the front tires lose authority. The first vehicle is complete when one light chest returns safely—not when every available part fits on the frame.

sections.heading: Upgrade by Route, Not by Decoration
bullets: Rough road: add four Off-Road Suspension units and retest rollover behavior.
Long night route: protect fuel and add two Switch-controlled Headlights.
Second chest: extend the wheelbase before loading it.
Heavy tool head: move to a dedicated mining or harvesting chassis.

title: Controller and Automation Guide - Three Tested Machines
description: Use exact part bills and commissioning tests for an 8–12 plot watering gantry, an 8 × 14 Vacuum Pump harvester, and a 6 × 6 Piston elevator.
imageAlt: A complex logic-controlled machine in Scrap Mechanic
quickAnswer: Prove movement with a manual control, then add one Controller sequence and one safety layer. Start with FRM-03 watering, FRM-08 harvesting, or LOG-09 lifting; each has a fixed baseline, a dry test, and a failure condition that must pass before automatic operation.

sections.heading: Choose One Machine, Not One Box of Parts
paragraphs: The watering gantry removes repeated water passes, the Vacuum Pump harvester removes repeated pickup, and the Piston elevator solves vertical access. Their parts overlap, but their failure conditions do not. Build the machine whose measured bottleneck already exists.

sections.heading: Commission Manual Movement First
steps: Build the moving frame and check its complete physical envelope.
Trigger motion from one manual control at the lowest speed.
Add the Controller only after the frame clears every edge.
Mark home, work, and stop states with paint.
Test obstruction and lost power before adding Sensors.

sections.heading: Watering: Count Missed Plots
paragraphs: A fast arm that misses one of twelve plots has failed. Run the two Pistons dry, water one fixed plot, then combine motion and delivery. Adjust Cannon height or row spacing before increasing speed, and preserve a bucket route beside the gantry.

sections.heading: Harvesting: Protect Storage Meaning
paragraphs: The Pump must be in In mode and connected to one dedicated Large Chest. A planting output should use a different container and a visibly different control. The harvest pass gets faster only after the chest count matches the mature crop count.

sections.heading: Elevator: Stop Outside the Crush Zone
paragraphs: Four Pistons move the 6 × 6 platform in matched pairs, but the external emergency Switch is what makes a jam recoverable. Test an off-center block load and a mid-travel stop before a mechanic steps onto the platform.

sections.heading: Add Sensors Last
bullets: A Sensor confirms a state; it does not repair bad geometry.
A Logic Gate should express one named condition, not hide an unexplained chain.
Status lights should show home, moving, and fault states where the operator can see them.
Every automatic cycle needs a manual stop and physical service access.

sections.heading: Creative Blueprint to Survival Creation
paragraphs: The Garage is the supported bridge for a creation designed in Creative or saved from another supported building context. Survival still pays for every block and part in the selected blueprint, so the transfer is a production job rather than a free spawn.

Start with a small unmodded vehicle. A simple four-wheel test proves that selection, chest connection, material counting, and assembly all work before a complex Workshop creation consumes a full supply run.

sections.heading: Read the Bill Before Gathering
paragraphs: The material list is calculated from the actual shapes in the selected creation. Paint, symmetry, or visual size does not determine the cost; the included blocks and interactive parts do.
bullets: Remove decorative mass that does not serve the Survival job.
Replace unavailable mod parts before collecting materials.
Check whether the creation depends on recipes that your current world has not unlocked.
Keep fuel, ammunition, and cargo outside the blueprint bill unless the creation itself requires those items.

sections.heading: Use Fill Chest Without Losing Track
steps: Empty unrelated items from the Garage Chest.
Select the blueprint and record the current shortages.
Carry the matching blocks and parts in the mechanic's inventory.
Use Fill Chest to transfer only missing quantities.
Review the bill again and load anything held in external storage.
Assemble, then move the finished creation away before preparing another blueprint.

sections.heading: Workshop Blueprints and Version Mismatch
paragraphs: A Steam Workshop subscription makes a creation available to the building interface; it does not guarantee that every part exists in the current Survival world. A legacy, modded, or newer-version shape can make the Garage reject an otherwise visible blueprint.
Open the creation in Creative first, remove unsupported parts, save a clean copy, and retry that copy. This isolates blueprint compatibility from a missing-material problem.
